note: Demands from the great houses. {lord}, {house}, {target} (a settlement) and {rival} (another house) are filled in. Ops: favour and grievance on the asking house, rivalGrievance and rivalFavour on the rival, othersGrievance on every other house, treasury, trust (M24 B: Love, was Trust), ambition, grant (target goes to the house), exempt (days without crown taxes), office (a council seat). Ignored, the default choice is taken.

land.title: A grant of land
land.text: {lord} asks that {target}, which borders the lands of {house}, be granted to the family in fee. It would round off the estate, he says, and secure the road.

exemption.title: An exemption from taxes
exemption.text: {lord} pleads poor harvests and dear soldiers, and asks that the lands of {house} pay no taxes to the crown for a year.

office.title: A seat on the council
office.text: {lord} would serve the crown on the royal council, and would very much like to be asked.

marriage.title: A royal match
marriage.text: {lord} proposes his daughter as a bride for a cousin of the crown, with a dowry of three hundred crowns. The other houses are watching.

revenge.title: A feud
revenge.text: {lord} accuses {rival} of burning a mill and driving off cattle. He demands the crown punish them.

choices.label: Tell them to settle it themselves

coin.title: A request for coin
coin.text: {lord} asks the crown for four hundred crowns to mend the walls of his seat and pay his men.
